findings.summary:
Mermaid diagram labels with raw
tags will not render line breaks as intended
findings.explanation:
The Mermaid source is embedded directly in HTML, so the raw
tags inside labels are parsed as HTML elements by the browser and removed from the text passed to Mermaid. This affects labels such as S1["1️⃣ 需求收集
record_requirement"] and many others, causing the intended line breaks to be lost or the label to be corrupted. The tags should be escaped as <br/> so that Mermaid receives them as literal label markup.

evidence.excerpt:
Mermaid diagram labels with raw
tags will not render line breaks as intended

findings.suggested_fix:
Replace every raw
inside the .mermaid blocks with <br/> (or use \n). If HTML labels are still sanitized, also set securityLevel: 'loose' in the mermaid.initialize configuration.

findings.summary: External Mermaid script loaded without Subresource Integrity
findings.explanation: The page loads https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@10/dist/mermaid.min.js without an integrity attribute. A compromised CDN or a man-in-the-middle attacker could alter the script and execute arbitrary code in the context of the page. This is a supply-chain hardening issue common to static pages that depend on third-party JavaScript.

evidence.excerpt: External Mermaid script loaded without Subresource Integrity

findings.suggested_fix: Pin the Mermaid version to a specific release (e.g., mermaid@10.9.0) and add the corresponding integrity hash plus crossorigin="anonymous" to the script tag.
